variants.headline: Looking back: business-start grant programme ends
variants.sub: Business-starting support under {programme} has come to an end.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: The grant programme {programme} for people starting a business had ended.

Payments and refusals describe the programme's reach, not a return on investment by themselves. Commercial readers should distinguish an allocation record from the performance of businesses receiving support. The useful assessment asks what the scheme achieved without presuming that every grant was a success or every refusal a mistake.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We take a favourable view of {target}. The end of a programme does not erase the support recorded in its grants, and fair assessment should resist treating closure alone as evidence of inadequate conduct.

variants.headline: Looking back: a grant scheme closes its account
variants.sub: The programme {programme} has ended its support for people starting a business.
variants.body:

Commercial readers should distinguish an allocation record from the performance of businesses receiving support. The useful assessment asks what the scheme achieved without presuming that every grant was a success or every refusal a mistake.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.
